crypto-lab-residue-gate.implementation: local BigInt arithmetic / isolated key-holder worker
crypto-lab-residue-gate.note: Read binary Jacobi, Euler Legendre, modular roots/CRT, Goldwasser–Micali encryption and the Rabin key-holder closure. The Tonelli anchor executes order halving; the Rabin anchor actually squares the validated message. A public attacker receives N and one root-query closure, never p/q. The canonical QR root oracle yields independently verified factors; redundancy can refuse or accidentally admit a query and is not called CCA security. One-bit Rabin is distinct from GM. crypto-lab-dvd-scramble.note: Source review of src/css/lfsr.ts, src/css/css.ts, src/attack/divide.ts and src/verify/verify.ts. lfsr.ts cites Boneh-Shoup v0.6 section 3.8 Figure 3.10 and computes a bit-serial LFSR: step() returns bit 0, XORs the declared taps, right-shifts and feeds back into the top bit; byte() clocks eight steps LSB- or MSB-first. css.ts generate() seeds a 17-bit register with taps [14,0] and a 25-bit register with taps [12,4,3,0], clocks a byte from each and adds them with carry, so z = (x+y+carry) mod 256 and the carry persists -- the CSS byte-serial combiner. The key space is 16 bits plus 24 bits, validated as such, which is the 40 bits the attack exhibit is about. divide.ts recover() enumerates smaller-register seeds and returns counted candidates; verify.ts checks a candidate against continuation bytes the search never saw. Zero runtime dependencies. N/A means no named algorithm IN THIS INDEX, not no computation: the Content Scrambling System and the LFSR family are outside the current vocabulary, the same reason crypto-lab-lfsr-forge was reviewed N/A on 2026-10-09. Scope recorded with it: this is the textbook generator, and the source says so in its own extension note -- deployed CSS changes insertion positions, discards early bytes and has inverter modes, none of which are implemented here. So the card must not be read as a deployed-CSS implementation.
